background: In September 2026, the German political party Alternative für Deutschland (AfD) suffered a data breach which exposed 345k unique email addresses. The following month, hundreds of gigabytes of data containing hundreds of thousands of emails and attachments was published online, with searchable AI-generated summaries and downloadable original files.

An analysis of the incident reported that the breach was detected as early as 9 September, with a subsequent intrusion occurring five days later. In its public statement , AfD attributed the breach to an attack on a hosting provider, identified in subsequent reporting as the party-owned Alternita Dienstleistungs GmbH.
how: The published account does not explain the exact way the data was obtained.
outcome: 345,439 accounts are listed in this breach. This is a count of accounts, not necessarily individual people.
The reported exposed data includes Email addresses, Email messages.
editorial: Two data classes, but one of them is "email messages", and that is the part that matters. An email address list tells you who was on a mailing list. Hundreds of gigabytes of messages and attachments tell you what people wrote to a political party, which under European data protection law counts as special category data because it can reveal political opinions. Have I Been Pwned flags this entry as sensitive.

The publication format is new and worth watching. The data was released with searchable, AI-generated summaries alongside the original files. That lowers the effort needed to find a named person in a leak from days of reading to a single search, which makes the exposure for anyone who merely wrote in, including people who are not members, far greater than the headline count of addresses suggests.

The party attributed the breach to an attack on its hosting provider. Whatever one thinks of the organisation, the lesson is general: correspondence sent to any campaign, charity or advocacy group sits on someone else's servers indefinitely. If you are in this set, assume messages you sent could be quoted back to you, and treat any contact that references them with caution.

actions: Be alert to phishing. A message may use details from exposed or collected records to appear familiar; verify requests through the service directly.
